policy.policy_0_3: Deploy rapid drought contingency plans in Afar, Somali, and Oromia. Restrict non-essential water usage, regulate dam releases weekly, and provide targeted emergency food aid. Early warning SMS alerts to farmers.
policy.policy_3_6: Expand irrigation coverage with solar-powered pumps, subsidize drought-resistant seeds (sorghum, millet, teff), and establish regional grain reserves. Coordinate hydropower production with rainfall outlook.
policy.policy_6_12: Scale up community water harvesting projects, diversify energy mix (hydro + solar + wind), and strengthen regional food trade agreements. Train farmers in conservation agriculture practices.
policy.policy_12_18: Invest in long-term resilience: large-scale reservoir expansion, reforestation, and cross-border water-sharing treaties. Integrate carbon credit programs to fund climate-smart agriculture.
policy.policy_sources: Generated by Admas AI ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM), trained on FAO, WFP, IPCC, and Ethiopian MoA guidelines.
policy.rule_1: Policies must adapt dynamically as new model forecasts (0–18M) are updated every month.
policy.rule_2: Short-horizon (0–6M) actions always take priority over long-horizon plans.
policy.rule_3: Decisions are based on ensemble confidence: if Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM disagree, human expert validation is required.
policy.rule_4: Water allocation follows basin-level hydrological balance and AI-simulated scenarios.
policy.rule_5: Energy planning must ensure hydropower reliability under predicted drought stress.
policy.rule_6: All AI outputs are explainable (via SHAP/XAI), ensuring transparency for policymakers.

platform.simulation_notice: Dashboard metrics and generated forecast outputs are simulated, not validated live predictions.
